title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #3

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What comes out of a bean seed first when it starts to grow? (1 mark)
   A. A flower
   B. A root
   C. A fruit
   D. A new seed

2. Which is the best way of studying how a seedling grows? (1 mark)
   A. Never water it
   B. Pull it up daily
   C. Measure its height every two days
   D. Cover it in sand

3. Which of these is an insect? (1 mark)
   A. Snail
   B. Earthworm
   C. Crab
   D. Butterfly

4. Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing it with flies
   B. Putting it on the floor
   C. Leaving it uncovered in the sun
   D. Covering it and keeping it clean

5. How often should teeth be brushed? (1 mark)
   A. Once a month
   B. At least twice a day
   C. Once a year
   D. Never

6. Where does digestion finish and digested food pass into the blood? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Small intestine
   C. Mouth
   D. Stomach

7. What is diarrhoea? (1 mark)
   A. A swollen stomach
   B. Food coming out of the mouth
   C. Passing hard dry faeces
   D. Passing loose watery faeces many times

8. What is saliva? (1 mark)
   A. A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   B. A type of waste
   C. A tube in the stomach
   D. A germ

9. Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Liquid
   C. Powder
   D. Solid

10. Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses? (1 mark)
   A. They keep their shape and can support weight
   B. They are invisible
   C. They flow easily
   D. They spread out

11. Which state of matter has its own shape and fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Solid
   B. Steam only
   C. Liquid
   D. Gas

12. Which of these solids can be poured? (1 mark)
   A. Flour
   B. Stone
   C. Brick
   D. Ruler

13. What does recycle mean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste away
   B. Bury waste
   C. Make waste into new things
   D. Burn waste

14. What is a compost pit used for? (1 mark)
   A. Storing glass
   B. Storing plastic
   C. Turning kitchen waste into manure
   D. Burning waste

15. Who should monitor taps in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Water monitors
   B. Nobody
   C. Only cooks
   D. Only visitors

16. Which of these is an example of reducing water wastage? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving the hose on
   B. Washing with lots of water
   C. Closing a tap after use
   D. Ignoring leaks

17. Which of these is NOT an effect of force? (1 mark)
   A. Stopping motion
   B. Changing shape
   C. Making something have colour
   D. Starting motion

18. Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope? (1 mark)
   A. Magnetism only
   B. Gravity
   C. Sound
   D. Light

19. Logs placed under a heavy load help it move because they act as (1 mark)
   A. Brakes
   B. Glue
   C. Weights
   D. Rollers

20. Why do matches light when rubbed on the box? (1 mark)
   A. Friction makes cold
   B. Wind makes fire
   C. Gravity makes light
   D. Friction makes heat

21. A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because (1 mark)
   A. The stone is lighter
   B. The paper is heavier
   C. Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   D. There is no gravity

22. What is a force? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of sound
   B. A kind of light
   C. A push or a pull
   D. A kind of matter

23. A wheelbarrow is easier to move than dragging a load because (1 mark)
   A. Gravity is less
   B. The wheel reduces friction
   C. The load gets smaller
   D. The wheel is heavy

24. Which of these is opaque? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water
   B. Clear plastic
   C. Wood
   D. Clear glass

25. What does light help us to do? (1 mark)
   A. Taste
   B. Hear
   C. See
   D. Smell

26. Which wall colour helps a room to be brighter? (1 mark)
   A. Dark blue
   B. Dark brown
   C. Dark black
   D. Light colours

27. Which of these is a safety use of light? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Street lights
   C. Making sound
   D. Colouring paint

28. Which of these uses sunlight to dry things? (1 mark)
   A. Drying clothes and grain
   B. Making rain only
   C. Making ice
   D. Making stones

29. What does a mother hen do for her chicks? (1 mark)
   A. Feeds them iron
   B. Makes them wet
   C. Cools them
   D. Keeps them warm under her wings

30. Why should electric irons be unplugged after use? (1 mark)
   A. To prevent burns and fire
   B. To make them heavier
   C. To make them hot
   D. To make them noisy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how you would do an activity to show gravity. (4 marks)

32. Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference. (5 marks)

33. What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull. (2 marks)

34. Compare solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume. (4 marks)

35. Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm. (5 marks)

36. Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features. (4 marks)

37. Explain the difference between diarrhoea and constipation. (4 marks)

38. Explain how light helps in security and safety. Give three examples. (3 marks)

39. Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe. (5 marks)

40. Describe how you can show that rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones. (3 marks)

41. List four signs of life in plants. (2 marks)

42. Explain how drip irrigation and mulching save water. (4 marks)

43. Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment. (3 marks)

44. What happens in the large intestine? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A root
   The root comes out first and grows down into the soil.

2. C — Measure its height every two days
   Measuring height regularly shows growth over time.

3. D — Butterfly
   A butterfly has six legs and three body parts.

4. D — Covering it and keeping it clean
   Covered food is safer from germs.

5. B — At least twice a day
   Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

6. B — Small intestine
   The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs food into the blood.

7. D — Passing loose watery faeces many times
   Diarrhoea means loose watery faeces.

8. A — A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   Saliva wets food and starts to digest starchy foods.

9. A — Gas
   Gases spread out to fill all the space.

10. A — They keep their shape and can support weight
   Solids keep their shape.

11. A — Solid
   Solids keep their shape and volume.

12. A — Flour
   Flour is made of tiny solid grains that can pour.

13. C — Make waste into new things
   Recycling makes new things from old materials.

14. C — Turning kitchen waste into manure
   Decomposable waste rots into compost.

15. A — Water monitors
   Monitors help make sure taps are closed.

16. C — Closing a tap after use
   Closing taps stops the flow of water.

17. C — Making something have colour
   Colour is not caused by a force.

18. B — Gravity
   Gravity pulls water downhill.

19. D — Rollers
   Rollers reduce friction.

20. D — Friction makes heat
   Rubbing produces heat.

21. C — Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

22. C — A push or a pull
   A force is a push or a pull.

23. B — The wheel reduces friction
   Wheels roll and reduce friction.

24. C — Wood
   Wood blocks light.

25. C — See
   Light lets us see objects.

26. D — Light colours
   Light colours reflect more light.

27. B — Street lights
   Street lights help people see at night.

28. A — Drying clothes and grain
   Sunlight dries wet things.

29. D — Keeps them warm under her wings
   Chicks need warmth.

30. A — To prevent burns and fire
   Switching off prevents accidents.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drop a stone and a ball from the same height. Observe that they fall down to the ground. Gravity pulls them down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for items, 1 mark for dropping, 1 mark for observing downward fall, 1 mark for conclusion.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solid: own shape and fixed volume. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume. Gas: no shape and no fixed volume, fills the container.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each state with correct shape and volume, plus 1 mark for a comparison.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four features.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Diarrhoea is passing loose watery faeces many times and causes loss of water. Constipation is passing hard dry faeces with difficulty.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each condition.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Street lights help people see, security lights keep thieves away, traffic lights direct drivers, torches show dangers, reflectors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Slide the same block down a ramp covered with different surfaces. It travels a shorter distance on rough surfaces than on smooth ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drip irrigation sends water drop by drop to the roots so little is lost. Mulch covers soil so less water evaporates.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each method.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is taken back from the leftover food and the rest becomes faeces.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and 1 mark for faeces.
